events.text: Order placed for five 38 class locomotives with Clyde Engineering.

evidence.quote: In May 1939 , an order for five 38 class locomotives was placed with Clyde Engineering .
Constructed between January 1943 and November 1949 , the 30 locomotives in the class were designed

events.text: Decision made to purchase 25 more locomotives after the initial five.

evidence.quote: As the last of the five initial locomotives were leaving the shop in 1945 , a decision was made to purchase more

events.label: withdrawal
events.text: First class locomotive withdrawn from service.

evidence.quote: The first 38 class locomotive was withdrawn in 1961

events.text: Class briefly returned to the former Melbourne Limited Express route.

evidence.quote: The 38 class briefly returned to the former Melbourne Limited Express route in April 1962

events.text: Class ceased operating the Newcastle Flyer between Gosford and Newcastle.

evidence.quote: the Newcastle Flyer between Gosford and Newcastle until December 1970

events.label: withdrawal
events.text: Last class locomotive withdrawn from service.

evidence.quote: with the last withdrawn in December 1970

undated_mentions: Class first conceived in the 1930s when a need for a locomotive to eliminate double heading was established
Class repainted green after the war
Class repainted black in the 1950s (all except 3813)
Green livery restored to 3801 and 3830 in the 1960s
Class began handing some express services over to diesel locomotives in the 1950s
Central West Express operated by the class into the 1960s
